source.description:
Layer: core
Strategy: unit (example-based) + edge cases
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.3 (rank), xtrm-2azdj.4 (compare), xtrm-2azdj.5 (recommend)

What implementation it covers: the pure, non-CLI functions each verb factors out per its bead's SCOPE — rankModels(cache, capability), compareModels(cache, slugs), recommendForRole(cache, specialistModel). These take plain data in, return plain data/strings out, no file I/O, no network, no commander.

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/models-rank.test.ts, models-compare.test.ts, models-recommend.test.ts (or a single models-core.test.ts if the three functions are small enough to share a file — match whatever granularity cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts uses for a comparable module).

Assertions required:
- [ ] rankModels: sorts descending by the requested capability index; ties broken deterministically (stable order, no crash on equal values); rejects/errors on an unrecognized capability string before touching data.
- [ ] rankModels: never emits a blended/composite score field — assert the output object/row only carries the three raw indices + pricing, never a computed average.
- [ ] compareModels: all-slugs-found path returns rows in the same order as the input slugs (not cache iteration order).
- [ ] compareModels: partially-unmatched-slugs path returns a distinguishable "not found" marker for the missing slug's row/warning, while still returning full rows for the found ones (does not throw, does not silently drop the whole request).
- [ ] recommendForRole: exact/normalized match found → correct rank position computed against the full cache (e.g. "4th of 23"), and the alternative-suggestion logic only fires when a genuinely higher-ranked model exists (no suggestion when the current model is already top-ranked).
- [ ] recommendForRole: no match found → returns the graceful fallback data (top N agentic_index entries) rather than throwing or returning empty/undefined.
- [ ] Edge cases: empty cache (zero models) for all three functions — must return an empty-but-valid result / clear "no data" signal, not throw.
- [ ] Edge cases: single-model cache for rank/recommend (rank position is trivially 1st of 1; no alternative to suggest).

Fixture policy:
- [ ] No shared mutable state between tests — construct a fresh fake cache object per test.
- [ ] Deterministic fixtures — hand-written small cache arrays (3-5 fake models with known index values), no reliance on real cached data or the live repo's specialist files.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not tautological: rank/compare/recommend expected outputs are computed independently in the test (e.g. by pre-sorting the fixture by hand), not derived from calling the function under test itself.
- [ ] Not over-mocked: nothing here should mock internal collaborators — these are pure functions, call them directly.

Critical paths covered:
- Never-blend-scores invariant — risk: violating the epic's core design promise (separate capability axes) silently regresses to a misleading single score.
- recommend's no-match fallback — risk: a naming-scheme mismatch between specialist execution.model strings and OpenRouter permaslugs is the expected common case (flagged in xtrm-2azdj.5's CONSTRAINTS), so this path WILL be hit in real usage and must never crash.

Known deferred paths:
- Property-based/fuzz testing of arbitrary cache shapes — deferred, example-based fixtures are sufficient for v1 given the small, well-typed cache schema from xtrm-2azdj.1.

Debuggability evidence required: none beyond standard test failure output — these are pure functions with no logging contract of their own.

Done when: all assertions above pass in `npm test --workspace cli`, and removing any one of rank's sort-by-capability logic, compare's unmatched-slug handling, or recommend's fallback branch causes at least one test to fail (verify by temporarily reverting the relevant logic during test authoring).
source.title: Test: rank/compare/recommend core logic — unit tests
